definitions.explanation: A particle used with negative verbs to express 'only' or 'nothing but.' The verb following しか must be in negative form.

examples.japanese: ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧しか⟦{飲|の}まない→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。

examples.english: I rarely see (them) / I only see (them) on rare occasions.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧しか⟦{話|はな}せない→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。

notes:
しか is a restrictive particle meaning "only" that is always followed by a negative predicate.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- X しか + negative = only X: ⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧しか⟦{来|こ}なかった→来る：00254_kuru⟧ (only one person came)
- ⟦これ→これ：00963_kore⟧しか⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ (this is all there is)
- dictionary form + しか⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ = have no choice but to: ⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧しか⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ (all we can do is wait)

WATCH OUT:
- しか replaces ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ and ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ (⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧しか⟦{飲|の}まない→飲む：00322_nomu⟧, not ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧しか), but follows other particles: ⟦{日曜日|にちようび}→日曜日：00656_nichiyoubi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧しか⟦{会|あ}えない→会う：00482_au⟧ (can only meet on Sundays).
- The predicate is negative even though the English is positive: "I only have 100 yen" is {百円|ひゃくえん}しか⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧: neutral "only", used with positive or negative predicates. しか stresses that the amount falls short of what was wanted or expected.
  - ⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{来|き}た→来る：00254_kuru⟧: Only one person came. (neutral)
  - ⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧しか⟦{来|こ}なかった→来る：00254_kuru⟧: Only one person came. (fewer than hoped)
